claim_map.claim: Cone mode includes files under listed dirs at any depth plus files that are siblings of the listed dir or any ancestor.
claim_map.verbatim: all files under the specified directories (at any depth) will be included in the sparse checkout, as well as files that are siblings of either the given directory or any of its ancestors

claim_map.claim: Cone MODE HANDLING parent/toplevel inclusion rule.
claim_map.verbatim: For any directory specified, all paths below that directory will be included, and any paths immediately under leading directories (including the toplevel directory) will also be included.

claim_map.claim: Sparse checkout changes which tracked files are present in the working tree.
claim_map.verbatim: create sparse checkouts, which change the working tree from having all tracked files present to only having a subset of those files

claim_map.claim: --filter=blob:none filters blobs until needed by Git; later fetching possible.
claim_map.verbatim: --filter=blob:none will filter out all blobs (file contents) until needed by Git

claim_map.claim: --depth creates a shallow clone with truncated history.
claim_map.verbatim: Create a shallow clone with a history truncated to the specified number of commits.

claim_map.claim: reapply exists because merge/rebase can materialize extra paths; sparsify can fail on changed/conflicted files.
claim_map.verbatim: Commands like merge or rebase can materialize paths to do their work (e.g. in order to show you a conflict), and other sparse-checkout commands might fail to sparsify an individual file (e.g. because it has unstaged changes or conflicts).
Disable the core.sparseCheckout config setting, and restore the working directory to include all files.

claim_map.claim: Sparse index is optional, default-off, experimental index-size/performance feature.
claim_map.verbatim: Use the --[no-]sparse-index option to use a sparse index (the default is to not use it). A sparse index reduces the size of the index

claim_map.claim: --sparse sets up sparse checkout with only toplevel files initially.
claim_map.verbatim: Employ a sparse-checkout, with only files in the toplevel directory initially being present.

conditions_exceptions: Cone-mode claims apply to cone (default) mode with directory input; non-cone gitignore-pattern mode is deprecated and has different behavior.
reapply/disability behavior quoted from live manual; local-change protection (inspect/preserve/stop) is a product constraint (O5), stated as helper behavior, not as a git-manual guarantee.
Byte-bound rejection is inference from distinct control definitions plus absence of workload evidence, not a quoted manual sentence.
